result.summary: Reviewed git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex against the approved design doc (req029-node-attribute-edge-condition-validators.md) and REQ-028's already-merged style in the same file. (1) Idiomatic vs. crutch: idiomatic. validate_node_attributes/1 and validate_edge_conditions/1 use the exact same unconditional Enum.flat_map-over-check-list-then-concatenate composition as REQ-028's validate_graph/1 -- no early return, no case-based hand-rolled state logic, no crutch pattern. Every new private check_*/1 has the same uniform (t()) -> [Violation.t()] signature and @spec as REQ-028's check_*/1 functions; naming, comment-header style ('# CHK-NN: ...'), and doc cross-references to the design doc are consistent with the existing file. The ISO-8601 scan-forward parser and the CEL bracket/string/operator scanner are implemented as plain recursive/reduce_while stdlib functions (Regex, String, MapSet, Enum) -- no macros, no behaviours, no premature abstraction; this is idiomatic functional Elixir for a lexical scanner. (2) Supervision: N/A, explicitly confirmed rather than skipped -- grepped the diff and the full module for GenServer/gen_statem/Supervisor/spawn/Task/send/receive: zero hits. Letflow.Definitions.Graph remains a plain struct with zero-I/O pure functions (moduledoc's own purity contract, re-confirmed by this diff's own §8 grep: Repo./Logger./DateTime./File. all absent from executable code). No process, no InstanceSupervisor interaction, nothing to isolate. (3) Type-safety gaps: worth noting per the role's standing instruction even though not specifically asked. attributes is a bare map(); every check re-derives 'is this key present, right type, right shape' at runtime (is_binary/is_integer/is_map guards, Map.get with a catch-all _other -> true fallback) where a sum-typed language (Rust enum keyed on node_type carrying only the fields valid for that variant, or an OCaml GADT) would make 'a HUMAN_TASK node with a timeout_ms field but no role' inexpressible at construction time instead of merely un-flagged-until-validated at runtime. Same gap for Violation.code as a single flat 18-atom union rather than one refinement type per check family -- a stricter type system would tie each check's return code to that check's own variant at compile time. Both are consistent with the divergence REQ-028's design doc already accepted (Elixir has no static discriminated-union enforcement over a jsonb-sourced map) -- noting again here, not a new gap introduced by this diff, and not something to block on. (4) Scope creep: none found. The diff adds exactly the two public functions, one public helper, and the private plumbing the design doc specifies -- no REQ-030 create/1 pipeline code, no new Ecto/DB surface, no generic 'attribute schema' abstraction ahead of what CHK-09..17 need, no behaviour/macro machinery. The design doc's own explicit non-decisions (§9.2 unknown node_type handling, §9.3 REQ-030's two-call gap) were correctly left unresolved in the implementation rather than the implementer inventing a premature fix. docs/anti-patterns.md: none of its 3 entries apply to this diff (toolchain-availability, requirement_status.yaml overwrite, timestamp-drift are all process/bookkeeping issues unrelated to this pure-function code change) -- checked explicitly, not skipped. Reconstructed-algorithm spot-check (the task's specific focus): manually traced valid_iso8601_duration?/1 and valid_cel_syntax?/1 by hand against the design doc's own worked examples in §4.3 and §6, reading the merged source directly rather than trusting ELIXIR-DEV's self-report. Traced: P1DT12H (valid, date+time tokens both consumed cleanly), PT (invalid, empty time_part after T caught by the `time_part != ""` guard), P (invalid, zero tokens caught by `count > 0`), P3D2Y (invalid, wrong order correctly hits the {_before, []} :error branch in scan_duration_tokens's split_while), PXD (invalid, regex ^([0-9]+)([A-Za-z]) requires a leading digit, correctly fails to match and returns :error), and the CEL examples 'status == "approved"' (valid), 'status == ' (invalid, trailing bare '==' token caught), '(status == "approved"' (invalid, unclosed bracket), and the no-evaluation demonstration string (accepted, confirming the scanner never resolves variable identity). Every hand-traced case matched the design doc's stated expected result -- ELIXIR-DEV's divergence-free claim holds up on independent read, not just on the implementer's own say-so. No crutch or unjustified shortcut found in either reconstructed algorithm: both are total, deterministic, stdlib-only scanners that implement exactly the rules the design doc §4.3/§6 spelled out, with the design's own explicitly-flagged uncertainty (not verified against unreachable R-Co source) carried forward faithfully rather than silently smoothed over. Also confirmed: check_single_default_edge/1's Map.fetch!(node_index, edge.source) cannot raise in practice because it only runs on edges already filtered through exclusive_gateway_source?/3 (which requires a resolvable source), so the total/defensive claim in the moduledoc holds end-to-end. Verdict: PASS -- idiomatic, no supervision surface, type-safety gaps noted but inherited/expected rather than newly introduced, no scope creep, anti-patterns checked, reconstructed algorithms verified sound by independent trace.
